subject: Discovery recap: dedicated GPU pools & pilot fit — Neptune Analytics
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: David Li <david.li@neptuneanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: dedicated GPU pools & pilot fit — Neptune Analytics

Hi David — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so the team has one place to refer back to. Please call out anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Unpredictable inference TPS during end-of-month reporting windows, spikes 3–4x baseline, causing queueing and timeouts.
- Current self-hosted Triton/K8s setup is brittle during bursts and you lack clear isolation between models for different customers.
- Cost per inference is higher than expected due to small instances and limited batching; team wants to bring down unit cost without degrading p95 latency.
- Compliance: EU data residency for certain customers and auditability (detailed request logs + KV cache lifecycle).

Current stack + constraints
- Triton behind K8s with mixed GPU types (NVIDIA A10s + some older V100s).
- Serving mostly Mistral-175B family / Llama variants; typical prompt sizes ~512 tokens, average response ~120 tokens.
- Peak concurrent requests observed: ~220 sustained; occasional bursts up to ~900 QPS for 15–30 minutes.

Success criteria you outlined
- Predictable baseline throughput: 1,000 QPS sustained at 512-token context with p95 < 250ms (generation time for typical prompts).
- Isolation: model pools per tenant group to prevent noisy-neighbor issues and provide separate audit logs.
- Autoscale/burst behavior: ability to absorb short bursts (up to 3–4x baseline for 10–30 minutes) without dropping below p95 SLOs.
- Clear visibility into per-token cost and per-route latency breakdowns.

Recommended fit & immediate next steps (what Redwood will do)
1) I attached a capacity_sizing_template.xlsx — please fill in the highlighted tabs with: typical batch sizes, token distribution, concurrency by route, and expected growth. This will let us size a reserved pool proposal.
2) Proposed pilot: reserved GPU pool (4x A100-80GB initially) with prefix caching enabled + KV eviction policy tuned to your workload. Pilot scope: run production traffic for 2 weeks with throttled routing to validate p95 and unit cost. Estimated pilot timeline: 4–6 weeks from template completion.
3) Autoscale/burst policy options: we can configure a short-duration burst window (10–30 minutes) with pre-warmed burst capacity and automatic fallback to a smaller/cheaper model variant if sustained. I’ll sketch a baseline config in a follow-up.
4) Compliance checklist: we’ll share SOC 2 and audit-log export details (Marissa will follow up).
5) Tech deep-dive: schedule an infra session with your engineering lead to go over KV caching and network/topology (link below).

Asks for you
- Please return the sizing template by EOD next Wednesday (2027-05-26).
- Confirm the 900 QPS burst number is the 95th percentile peak and whether those bursts are typically 10–30 minutes.
- Share an internal contact (infra lead) for the tech deep-dive.

I'll follow up with a proposed pilot schedule and a rough pricing baseline once I have the completed template.

Cheers,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: capacity_sizing_template.xlsx, redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf
From: David Li <david.li@neptuneanalytics.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: dedicated GPU pools & pilot fit — Neptune Analytics

Jonas — thanks for the thorough summary. Quick clarifications:
- The 900 QPS number is correct for peak events but those are usually bursts of ~20 minutes tied to our end-of-month ingestion jobs. Baseline is ~250 QPS.
- We do need strict tenant isolation for our EU customers; that requirement is non-negotiable.
- Our infra lead is Alex Moreno (cc'ed on this thread in the next message) — he'll want to dig into network segmentation and whether the pool can be placed in our VPC with customer-managed subnets.

Two questions for your sizing template:
1) For token distribution, should we provide raw samples or aggregated percentiles?
2) On burst capacity — are we limited to a fixed number of GPUs for burst, or can Redwood provision ephemeral VMs to handle minute-scale spikes?

Appreciate you moving quickly on this.

Best,
David
VP of Engineering
Neptune Analytics
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: David Li <david.li@neptuneanalytics.com>, Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@neptuneanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: dedicated GPU pools & pilot fit — Neptune Analytics

David / Alex — thanks. Alex, great to e-meet — would love to schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive next week focused on: network placement (VPC peering / customer subnets), KV cache lifecycle, and autoscale knobs. I'll drop a calendar invite after this thread.

Answers to your questions:
1) Token distribution: aggregated percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) are fine for sizing; include a few raw samples if you see pathological prompts (very long contexts) so we can model tail behavior.
2) Burst capacity model: for Dedicated we offer two approaches — (a) reserved+burst pool where burst capacity is pre-allocated (recommended when you want strict performance guarantees), or (b) a hybrid model that allows ephemeral GPU capacity spun up in your VPC for short bursts. The hybrid option reduces committed cost but adds a brief provisioning window (30–90s) which may impact p95 for the first requests during a cold burst.

For your 20-minute bursts, our recommended approach is reserved baseline capacity sized for the p95 sustained load with a small pre-warmed burst buffer (e.g., +30–50% GPUs) to cover the first 10–15 minutes, plus a hybrid fallback for sustained spikes. That combination keeps latency predictable while keeping committed spend reasonable.

I attached a proposed-pilot-schedule.pdf that maps out milestones (template -> tech deep-dive -> pilot spin-up -> validation -> review).

Proposed next actions
- Alex: share p50/p95/p99 token percentiles + a few sample prompts by 2027-05-26.
- David: confirm whether you prefer pre-warmed burst capacity (higher commit, lower cold-starts) or hybrid ephemeral approach.
- Redwood (Marissa): share SOC2 docs and compliance artifact list.

I'll create the HubSpot MAP and add the pilot milestones — link below.

Thanks,
Jonas
